pr_title: Configure Scrape Interval and Timeout Via Relabeling
pr_body:

This PR adds the labels `__scrape_interval__` and `__scrape_timeout__` to configure the scrape interval and timeout of a target.

Fixes #8895
pr_comments: Just realized I forgot the UI component of this, I'll get to it later.

So the current scrape interval and timeout are already shown in the UI through their labels when hovering over the `Labels` box. It might be a good idea to add a separate column (or columns) for them though because you have to know where to look. Thoughts?
My idea was to have them with a tooltip on the last scrape duration
Ok, I added that in.

I still need to add tests and stuff in reload, but here's my plan now: In `sync`, the interval and timeout of the scrape loop are set directly from the `__scrape_interval__` and `__scrape_timeout__`, which themselves are initialized with the config values and remain that value unless changed by relabeling. In `reload`, we first check if the interval and timeout differ from the previous config. If they have, that means they've been set with relabeling and we should keep them that way, even if the new config specifies different values. If they haven't, we just use the new config.
Did you notice `func populateLabels(lset labels.Labels, cfg *config.ScrapeConfig) (res, orig labels.Labels, err error) {` ? That where we should set the labels.

Yup, that's where I'm setting them.

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/c44283b420173579e8781c3314247c6434e34048/scrape/target.go#L328-L336

On reload, there can be a new scrape interval and timeout, so we want to apply that to the targets, unless a target has set its own interval and timeout through relabeling. Then, we should just leave it alone. My problem is we have no current way of knowing if the targets have set their scrape interval and timeout through relabeling. We could just check if they still have the same timeout and interval as the previous configuration, but then what if they had set their interval and timeout to the same values of that configuration. We would then want to keep those values because they're what the target requested, but label-wise, it is undistinguished from other targets which are using the timeout and interval from the configuration. I think the only option would be to run `populateLabels` (which performs relabeling) again during a reload, but that seems wasteful.

> On reload, there can be a new scrape interval and timeout, so we want to apply that to the targets, unless a target has set its own interval and timeout through relabeling. Then, we should just leave it alone. My problem is we have no current way of knowing if the targets have set their scrape interval and timeout through relabeling. We could just check if they still have the same timeout and interval as the previous configuration, but then what if they had set their interval and timeout to the same values of that configuration. We would then want to keep those values because they're what the target requested, but label-wise, it is undistinguished from other targets which are using the timeout and interval from the configuration. I think the only option would be to run `populateLabels` (which performs relabeling) again during a reload, but that seems wasteful.

I propose we work on this specific problem separately. Maybe open an issue so we do not forget.

I think this is critical to the feature though. Without a solution, either we completely forget the relabeled interval and timeout on reload, or we don't apply the configurations new interval and timeout to any target on reload (this is probably worse). Either way, it's a bug.

Just a drive-by question:

> unless a target has set its own interval and timeout through relabeling.

Does this mean this PR does implement custom scrape intervals coming from actual instrumentation labels now? Or with "set its own interval", do you just mean that an individual target's target labels have an interval setting?
This PR aims to allow one to set the scrape interval and target via relabeling target labels coming from a target.
Ok, I guess it's the "coming from a target" that is ambiguous: I guess you mean coming from the target object, not from the actual scraped metrics, right?

Yup, sorry if that was unclear.

Like the ones in the labels column on the targets page.
Yup, ok :) Just wanted to make sure!

It seems like this requires documentation, plus the check for the interval smaller than the timeout.

Additionally, let's mark this as experimental, in case we change some semantics later.

Yeah, I started some changes but have been neglecting this for the past few days. We still need to figure out the reloading issue too.

I think the easiest solution would be to run relabeling again on reload, but I hate to run it again when we already have results.

Actually, I think it might be necessary to run relabeling on config reload. Because users could theoretically set different actions for different values of `__scrape_interval__` and `__scrape_timeout__`, we'd have to rerun their relabel configs when we change those labels.
If the base values change, then reload is not called for that target, a new one is created, if I am correct.
Oh, I see what you mean. Yes, there is something to investigate here. While investigating, we should cover blind spots with additional tests.

Yeah, don't think a new target is created when the interval or timeout is changed.

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/fa6b2897f0db5844cb7a2c6b4f17f3bd5a3deed4/scrape/scrape.go#L410-L439

I've addressed some of @roidelapluie's review comments and added relabeling on reload, as well as tests for it. I'm going to ignore the UI component and the documentation for now until we can agree on this part of the implementation.

We might want to consider moving the interval and timeout somewhere out of the tooltip on the last scrape duration because you'd never know it's there. Even I forgot for a second where it was just now. Maybe it gets its own box or is nestled into the same one as the last scrape duration.

> It seems like this requires documentation

I agree, but where would we put it?

Related: https://github.com/prometheus/docs/issues/1951#issuecomment-875192148

> Can you please also adapt the documentation?

Docs should go here https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/configuration/#relabel_config
@roidelapluie friendly ping :)
:100: thanks!!!!
Thanks so much for all your time reviewing! This one took a while.

@beorn7 FYI this feature is marked experimental and does not have a feature flag.

The reason for marking as experimental is the refusal to scrape when the scrape timeout > scrape interval. While I think we do the right thing here, I do not exclude that we revisit this, change or improve in the future.

In general, I would prefer to use feature flags for all experimental features (where that's reasonably possible), for simple consistency. If we only expect minor changes to the semantics, I can also live without the feature flag as we don't expect to change the behavior fundamentally or completely rip out the feature, i.e. most users of the experimental feature will probably be able to continue to use it in the way they use it for the lifetime of v2.x.

But as said, I would have preferred a feature flag here (but changing it now wouldn't be worth the hassle).

> The reason for marking as experimental is the refusal to scrape when the scrape timeout > scrape interval.

Perhaps we should indicate that in the docs then.

issue_context.title: Configurabe scrape interval / scrape timeout via relabeling
issue_context.body:
As per dev summit:

```
CONSENSUS: We want to be able to configure scrape intervals via relabelling.
```

It means that each target can have its own scrape interval.

My proposal is:

- Enable dynamic scrape interval / timeout via relabeling.
- Scrape interval should be shown in the UI, maybe as a tooltip in the last scrape column.

Note: I have already implemented scrape_interval and scrape_timeout labels in https://github.com/prometheus/common/commit/3a13497dea8f64585868e4c4ad710735653d6344 to ease contributions.
